payload.task_text:
I work in the academic office and we want to review the grade distributions for our Spring 2014 courses and also collect student feedback through a survey.

First, please look up all courses from Spring 2014 in our learning management system. For each course, I need to analyze the assignment submissions to compute grade statistics: the average score, the median score, the pass rate (percentage of submissions with score >= 60), and the total number of distinct students who submitted graded work (count each student once).

Create an Excel file called "Grade_Distribution_Report.xlsx" in the workspace with two sheets. The first sheet called "Course Grades" should have columns Course_Code, Course_Name, Avg_Grade, Median_Grade, Pass_Rate, and Total_Students. Include one row per Spring 2014 course. The second sheet called "Summary" should have columns Metric and Value with rows for Total_Courses (number of Spring 2014 courses), Overall_Avg_Grade (average across all courses), Highest_Avg_Course (name of course with highest average grade), and Lowest_Avg_Course (name of course with lowest average grade). Write all computed numbers as plain numeric values (do not write Excel formulas), and use the course code and full course name as they appear in the learning management system.

Second, create a survey form titled "Spring 2014 Course Feedback Survey" to collect student opinions. The form should have at least 4 questions: overall satisfaction with the course (as a choice question with options Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor), teaching quality rating (as a choice question with options 1 through 5), how they found the workload (as a choice question with options Too Light, Manageable, Heavy, Overwhelming), and an open-ended suggestions question (as a text question, not required).

Finally, send an email from registrar@university.edu to students@university.edu with the subject "Spring 2014 Course Feedback Survey" informing students about the survey and encouraging them to participate.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, keep the large submission reads outside the main context with exactly one parallel collector wave, and let the main agent itself produce the workbook, the form and the email — no second wave.

The main agent resolves the accessible task workspace, calls canvas_list_courses(include_ended=true) once, and retains exactly the six Spring 2014 courses by full name/code (expected course_ids 6, 8, 12, 15, 19, 22). Validate unique course IDs, then dispatch one explore collector per course.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 6 explore sub-agents in parallel, one per literal Spring course. Every collector follows the same literal recipe with only its course substituted:

1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Collector for course_id=6 (course_code and course_name as listed). A strictly read-only Canvas collector: call canvas_list_student_submissions(course_id=6, per_page=100, page=1), then keep calling page=2,3,... while pagination.has_more is true. The tool result may be truncated in the chat preview — always read the FULL JSON from the output_path file given in the result. A submission counts as graded iff it has a non-null numeric score field and workflow_state == "graded". Scores are on a 0-100 percentage scale. Aggregate all graded submissions in one script execution and return ONLY the compact JSON {course_id:6, course_code, course_name, avg_score, median_score, pass_rate, total_students, graded_count, pages}, where avg_score/median_score are the mean/median of graded scores, pass_rate = 100 * count(score >= 60) / graded_count, and total_students = number of DISTINCT user_ids among graded submissions. Do not return the row set, write any workspace file, or modify Canvas.
2. explore 1 (enterprise-data-analyst 1): Collector for course_id=8 — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.
3. explore 2 (enterprise-data-analyst 2): Collector for course_id=12 — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.
4. explore 3 (enterprise-data-analyst 3): Collector for course_id=15 — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.
5. explore 4 (enterprise-data-analyst 4): Collector for course_id=19 — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.
6. explore 5 (enterprise-data-analyst 5): Collector for course_id=22 — same literal recipe, only the course substituted.

After Wave 1, verify all six handoffs in one single pass (never per-course iteration): exactly one handoff per course, non-null statistics, graded_count > 0. Compute the four Summary metrics from the six unrounded course averages: Overall_Avg_Grade as the equal-weight arithmetic mean of the six course averages (not a submission-weighted global average); Highest_Avg_Course / Lowest_Avg_Course by unrounded course averages with course_code ascending only as a tie-break; Total_Courses = 6.

The main agent then completes every output directly, with no further delegation: (a) build Grade_Distribution_Report.xlsx in the resolved workspace with exactly two sheets — "Course Grades" with header Course_Code, Course_Name, Avg_Grade, Median_Grade, Pass_Rate, Total_Students and one row per course, and "Summary" with header Metric, Value and the four metric rows — all values plain numbers (no Excel formulas), then read both populated ranges back; (b) call create_form(title="Spring 2014 Course Feedback Survey") exactly once, add the four required questions sequentially with exact types/options/required flags (satisfaction choice Excellent/Good/Fair/Poor; teaching-quality choice 1-5; workload choice Too Light/Manageable/Heavy/Overwhelming; open-ended optional text suggestions), and verify with get_form(formId); (c) search Sent mail for From registrar@university.edu, To students@university.edu, subject Spring 2014 Course Feedback Survey, send exactly once only if no exact match exists, and read the retained message back. Finally run ONE reconciliation turn covering the workbook read-back, the form ID and the sent message, then call claim_done. Do not dispatch any agent after Wave 1, do not add a verification wave, and do not expose raw submission rows to the main context.

You are planning a multi-part task for an academic office. Produce an ordered, detailed plan. Do NOT execute any writes — only read-only investigation and planning.

TASK DESCRIPTION (from the user):
1. In the Canvas LMS, look up all courses from Spring 2014 (term). For each course, analyze assignment submissions to compute grade statistics: average score, median score, pass rate (percentage of submissions with score >= 60), and total number of DISTINCT students who submitted graded work (count each student once).
2. Create an Excel file "Grade_Distribution_Report.xlsx" in the workspace directory /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-grade-distribution-gform/workspace with two sheets:
   - Sheet "Course Grades": columns Course_Code, Course_Name, Avg_Grade, Median_Grade, Pass_Rate, Total_Students — one row per Spring 2014 course. Use course code and full course name as they appear in the LMS.
   - Sheet "Summary": columns Metric and Value with rows: Total_Courses (number of Spring 2014 courses), Overall_Avg_Grade (average across all courses), Highest_Avg_Course (name of course with highest average grade), Lowest_Avg_Course (name of course with lowest average grade).
   - All numbers must be plain numeric values (no Excel formulas).
3. Create a Google Form titled "Spring 2014 Course Feedback Survey" with at least 4 questions:
   - Overall satisfaction (multiple choice: Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor)
   - Teaching quality rating (multiple choice: 1 through 5)
   - Workload (multiple choice: Too Light, Manageable, Heavy, Overwhelming)
   - Open-ended suggestions (text question, NOT required)
4. Send an email from registrar@university.edu to students@university.edu with subject "Spring 2014 Course Feedback Survey" informing students about the survey and encouraging participation.

AVAILABLE TOOLS (read-only for you):
- Canvas MCP tools (canvas_*): list courses (canvas_list_courses, canvas_list_account_courses), get course (canvas_get_course), list assignments (canvas_list_assignments), list assignment submissions (canvas_list_assignment_submissions, canvas_list_student_submissions), get course grades (canvas_get_course_grades), list account users, dashboard, etc.
- Google Forms MCP tools (google_forms_*): get_form, get_form_responses, etc. (read-only)
- Excel MCP tools (excel_*): read workbook metadata, read data (read-only)
- Filesystem MCP tools (filesystem_*): read/list/search only (read-only)
- Email MCP tools (emails_*): read emails, search, get folders (read-only)
- mcp__local__python_execute can run read-only python.

YOUR DELIVERABLE: A step-by-step plan. For each step specify:
- Dispatch decision: self (main agent), explore (read-only subagent), or coder (write-capable subagent)
- Whether the step is independent (parallelizable) or depends on a previous step's output
- Exact tool calls (with likely parameters) to use
- How to verify the step's output

KEY PLANNING QUESTIONS TO RESOLVE (investigate read-only as needed):
a) How to identify Spring 2014 courses: check canvas_list_courses / canvas_get_dashboard_cards / account courses — look for term/enrollment_term_id or course names/codes containing "Spring 2014" or similar. Investigate what courses exist and how their term is represented.
b) How to compute grade stats: For each course, list assignments, then list submissions per assignment (or canvas_list_student_submissions for the whole course). Determine which submissions count as "graded work" (e.g., workflow_state graded/submitted, score not null). Note that submissions may come from different assignment types; decide a consistent aggregation rule (e.g., consider all graded submissions across all assignments, or per-assignment scores). Pass rate = fraction of graded submissions with score >= 60. Distinct students = count of unique student user_ids among graded submissions.
c) What counts as "average score" — average across all graded submissions (pooled), and Overall_Avg_Grade for the Summary = average of course Avg_Grade values across courses (or pooled? decide and be consistent — recommend average of the per-course averages).
d) Whether the Excel file already exists in the workspace (check /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-grade-distribution-gform/workspace).
e) Whether a Google Form with that title already exists.
f) Email tool: send_email with from_addr=registrar@university.edu, to=students@university.edu.

Also verify the environment: run canvas_health_check, check email connection, list allowed directories. Report what you find.

Return the plan as structured text, including the ordered list of steps with dependencies, the exact tool sequences, and a verification strategy. Be concrete and specific.
Plan grade distribution task

You are a data-collection subagent for a grade distribution report. Your assigned Spring 2014 course is: 6|BBB-2014B|Biochemistry & Bioinformatics (Spring 2014) (format: course_id|course_code|course_name).

Context: We are compiling per-course grade statistics from Canvas assignment submissions for Spring 2014 courses. In this environment, submission scores are already normalized to a 0-100 scale (e.g., "100.00" or 67). 'Graded work' is defined as a submission with workflow_state == "graded" AND a non-null numeric score.

WORKSPACE (write files here): /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-canvas-grade-distribution-gform/workspace

STEPS:
1. Parse course_id, course_code, course_name from your item.
2. List assignments: mcp__canvas__canvas_list_assignments(course_id=<id>). Record the assignment ids.
3. Fetch ALL submissions for the course. Primary method: mcp__canvas__canvas_list_student_submissions(course_id=<id>, student_ids=["all"], per_page=100, page=1...N) — follow pagination (the response may include a pagination object with has_more / next_page; keep paging until has_more is false or no more pages). If that endpoint errors or returns nothing useful, fall back to per-assignment fetching: mcp__canvas__canvas_list_assignment_submissions(course_id=<id>, assignment_id=<a>, per_page=100, page=1...N) for each assignment, following pagination.
4. Accumulate every submission record. Keep at minimum these fields per submission: assignment_id, user_id, score, workflow_state.
5. Save the full raw submission list to raw_submissions_<course_id>.json in the workspace using mcp__filesystem__write_file (write a JSON array of the records).
6. Compute statistics with mcp__local__python_execute (load the JSON file in Python and compute):
   - graded = submissions where workflow_state == "graded" and score is not None and parses to a float
   - avg_grade = round(mean of all graded scores, 2)
   - median_grade = round(median of all graded scores, 2)
   - pass_rate = round(100 * (count of graded scores >= 60) / (count of graded scores), 2)  # percentage on 0-100 scale
   - total_students = number of DISTINCT user_id values among graded submissions
   - total_graded_submissions = len(graded)
   Use Python's statistics.mean / statistics.median. Handle string scores by float().
7. Write stats_<course_id>.json in the workspace via mcp__filesystem__write_file with keys: course_id, course_code, course_name, avg_grade, median_grade, pass_rate, total_students, total_graded_submissions.

RETURN in your final summary (be exact and complete): course_id, course_code, course_name, avg_grade, median_grade, pass_rate, total_students, total_graded_submissions, plus the absolute paths to the two JSON files you wrote, and any anomalies encountered (e.g., zero graded submissions, pagination problems, unexpected workflow_state values).

Sanity checks: total_students must be <= the course's total enrollment (for course 6 it is 1613; use canvas_get_course to confirm enrollment if unsure). If you find zero graded submissions, investigate the actual workflow_state values present and report them — do not silently return zeros.
Fetch submissions + compute stats per course
